title: Improvements for my Racing Game?
author: Swimming_Ask3859
selftext:
I've been building **REDLINE**, a browser-based 3D drone racing game using ChatGPT, and I'm looking for people to test the latest version and give feedback.

The game takes place in a large sandstone canyon with winding rivers, waterfalls, narrow passages, and obstacles designed around three-dimensional flight. You pilot a futuristic drone through checkpoints, dodge rocks and birds, use an afterburner for extra speed, and fire dual red lasers at destructible targets.

**How I used AI to develop it**

I've been using ChatGPT throughout development to help write and revise the JavaScript and Three.js code, implement gameplay systems, and troubleshoot rendering and physics problems.

One of the biggest challenges has been getting the canyon environment to look realistic while maintaining playable performance. I started with procedural terrain, but the walls looked far too smooth and artificial. I eventually incorporated PBR sandstone and riverside materials, added layered cliff geometry, and worked on improving the water rendering and river simulation.

The process hasn't been straightforward. Some improvements introduced new problems, including repeated rock textures, waterfalls clipping through canyon walls, and objects that looked solid but had no proper collisions.

Fixing these required multiple iterations. For example, I moved from approximate collision boundaries toward mesh-based collision detection and added checks to stop the drone from passing through rocks at high speeds. The waterfalls were another challenge because their geometry needed to follow the canyon without disappearing behind the terrain.

I also spent time refining the flight controls. The drone now has adjustable handling, directional leaning, animated tilt-rotor hoverpads, and a boost system. The laser mechanics were particularly interesting because the beams needed to originate from the moving drone while still firing in a predictable direction.

One thing I've learned is that AI can generate features surprisingly quickly, but getting those features to work together consistently is much harder. A change that improves the visuals can break collisions or performance, so testing and repeated corrections have been a major part of development.

**Where the game currently stands**

REDLINE is an early playable prototype, not a finished game. I'm still improving the environmental realism, racing mechanics, performance, and overall feel of flying through the canyon.

The game is free to play in a desktop browser, and I'd appreciate feedback from other developers, especially on:

* Whether the drone feels responsive and enjoyable to control.
* Whether the canyon and waterfalls look convincing.
* Whether the course has enough variety and interesting obstacles.
* Whether performance is acceptable on different hardware.
* What you would prioritize improving before adding more features.

**Playable build:** [redline-grand-gorge-v9.rainymorel7.chatgpt.site](http://redline-grand-gorge-v9.rainymorel7.chatgpt.site)

I'm particularly interested in hearing from people who've worked with Three.js, browser rendering, procedural terrain, or AI-assisted game development. I'd also love to know what approaches you've found useful for preventing new AI-generated changes from breaking previously working systems.

This is still very much a work in progress, and constructive criticism is welcome.
